The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voting Index (PVI) is a measure of how strongly a U.S. congressional district leans towards either the Democratic or Republican party. It is displayed as a letter (either D or R) followed by a plus sign and a number, with the number indicating the number of percentage points above the national average that the district voted for the party indicated by the letter. The PVI is calculated by looking at how the district voted in the past two presidential elections combined and comparing it to the national average. In 2022, the formula for calculating PVI values was updated to weigh the most recent presidential election more heavily.

Trans broken arm syndrome is a common form of discrimination in healthcare settings in which a doctor mistakenly assumes that a trans person's medical ailments stem from their trans status or gender-affirming care, leading to incorrect treatment or denial of care. Trans patients often hide their trans status when visiting a doctor if their problem is not related to their trans status, particularly in rural or conservative areas. A 2022 survey from the Center for American Progress found that 19% of trans individuals had experienced this form of discrimination in the past year.

Transgender people have the right to medical privacy, and medical providers and insurance companies are prohibited from disclosing any personal medical information, including a person's transgender status, under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). Transgender people are also entitled to access and receive a copy of their medical records from healthcare facilities under HIPAA. However, it can be difficult for transgender people to find insurance coverage for their medical needs, as hormone therapy and sex reassignment surgery are not always covered by insurance policies. Even when these treatments are covered, transgender people may face barriers to accessing them due to discrimination or lack of knowledge among healthcare providers.
